aiOverview.content: As of March 2026, new COVID-19 variants—specifically the highly mutated BA.3.2 (nicknamed "Cicada")—are spreading in the U.S. and globally. Despite the high number of mutations, symptoms remain similar to previous Omicron subvariants and are generally reported as mild to moderate in vaccinated individuals. Common Symptoms of Current COVID-19 Variants (2026): Runny or stuffed nose (often the first sign) Sore throat (described as severe, scratchy, or "razorblade throat" in some cases) Headache (often moderate, felt around the forehead or temples) Dry cough (mild but persistent) Fatigue or extreme tiredness Sneezing (increasingly common in recent variants) Body aches and muscle pain Fever or chills (less common than in earlier waves) Key Differences and New Trends: Cold-like Presentation: The new variants frequently present with upper respiratory symptoms that are difficult to distinguish from a common cold or flu. Loss of Taste/Smell: This symptom has become less common compared to earlier in the pandemic, although it can still occur. Shortened Incubation: Newer subvariants tend to have a shorter incubation period, with symptoms appearing 2–4 days after exposure compared to 5–7 days previously. Asymptomatic Spread: As with previous Omicron strains, BA.3.2 can cause asymptomatic infections. When to Seek Emergency Care:If you or a loved one experience any of the following, seek immediate medical attention: Difficulty breathing or severe shortness of breath Persistent chest pain or pressure New confusion or inability to wake up Bluish lips, skin, or nail beds Prevention and Treatment: Vaccines: The 2025-2026 COVID vaccines are expected to provide protection against severe disease from current strains. Treatment: The BA.3.2 variant remains sensitive to existing COVID antiviral drugs. Testing: Rapid antigen tests are still effective at detecting these new variants. Disclaimer: Health information is evolving. Check the CDC or local health department website for the most up-to-date information.
